Historical May norms hover near 18°C, underscoring this above-average warmth.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects high uncertainty in short-range forecasts for Milan's highest temperature on May 5, with implied probabilities tightly clustered around 14–17°C (over 34% each) amid overcast conditions and risk of showers capping daytime heating. Latest runs from ECMWF and GFS ensembles indicate northerly airflow ushering cooler air masses into northern Italy, with model spreads showing highs from 14°C in cloudier members to 17–18°C where breaks occur; Italian services like MeteoLive project peaks near 17–18°C under covered skies. This marks a cooldown from early May warmth, driven by a low-pressure system over central Europe noted in updates over the past 48 hours. New 12Z model outputs today and ARPA Lombardia observations tomorrow could refine cloud cover and boundary layer mixing, key differentiators between outcomes. Historical May 5 highs average 20°C, but current synoptic patterns favor subdued temperatures below climatology.
